newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeder cattle steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeder cattle steady.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle were expected to start about steady, livestock analysts said.
Some analysts look for carryover selling in live cattle after this week's slide in cash beef prices, lower cash cattle prices this week and expected lower packer bids next week.
However, others anticipate evening of positions ahead of the monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report Friday afternoon.

Estimates for on-feed supplies in the seven major states as of January 1 averaged 104.2 percent in a range of 102 to 105 percent of a year ago. December placement estimates averaged 108.2 per cent in a range of 103 to 112 percent and marketings estimates averaged 101.8 percent in a range of 99 to 107.1 percent of last year.
Feeder cattle were seen steady as a higher CME index could offset early calls for higher corn futures and the weak tone to fed cattle markets, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.11 at $70.21 per cwt, the highest since March 9, 1995.
